## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

```text
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the black Audi RS7 sportback in <Picture 1>, featuring gloss black paint beaded with rain, lit matrix LED headlights, a black front grille, black wheels, and a sleek sportback profile.
<Picture 1> is the first frame of [Shot 1], showing the black Audi RS7 sportback moving fast on a wet multi-lane highway in heavy rain, with a city skyline and green overhead signs in the background.

summary:
[keyframe completion] The target video begins from <Picture 1>, showing <Subject 1> driving fast on a wet highway in heavy rain. The car undergoes a fast mechanical disassembly into flying parts and then reassembles into one whole car while the camera performs a continuous 180-degree low tracking arc around it.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the black Audi RS7 sportback's gloss black paint, rain beading, lit matrix LED headlights, black grille, black wheels, and sportback shape are retained from <Picture 1>.
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the opening composition, wet highway, heavy rain, city skyline, green overhead signs, and the car's front-left three-quarter position are retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is a photoreal automotive VFX style with wet asphalt reflections, heavy rain streaks, and a cold cinematic color grade.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>, a low tracking view of <Subject 1>, the black Audi RS7 sportback with gloss black paint beaded with rain, lit matrix LED headlights, black grille, and black wheels, moving fast on a wet multi-lane highway in heavy rain. A city skyline and green overhead signs sit behind the car. The camera is a low 24mm wide tracking shot, about 0.5 m above the wet asphalt, starting 2 m off the car's front-left quarter and pacing the car at the same speed. It performs one continuous 180-degree arc from front-left three-quarter to rear-right three-quarter, with no cut, no zoom, and no crane. The car stays centered at about 45% frame height while rain streaks cross the foreground and road spray licks the lens. At the widest scatter, the motion ramps briefly into 0.3-second slow motion at 50% speed and returns to real time, with focus held on the still-moving chassis while flying parts pass softly out of focus in the foreground. Through the first part, the car holds its speed and comes apart fast along its own structure into a wide scatter: hood, fenders, doors, side glass, headlight units, grille, mirrors, rear spoiler, wheels, brake discs, exhaust, and engine block fly far outward and stay readable. Every piece keeps traveling forward with the car's momentum and turns as it leaves, while rain and road spray scatter with them in clean mechanical separation, with no collision and no fire. Through the middle, the pieces hold wide apart around the still-rolling chassis, opening a broad view of the inner frame, suspension, and empty wheel arches while the car continues moving forward. Through the last part, the same pieces travel back from that wide scatter along the same paths and seat into one whole car again while it keeps driving, completing the 180-degree orbit. The shot ends locked on the reassembled black car pulling away through the rain, spray trailing behind. No captions, titles, subtitles, or watermarks appear beyond markings already present in <Picture 1>.

overall_soundscape:
Heavy rain and tire spray, a deep engine pull, a fast metallic whoosh as the body opens, a brief low-pass hush during the slow-motion beat, panels and wheels clunking back into place from far out, and a soft low studio hum. No speech.

non_diegetic_music:
none.
```
